# 2 Samuel Chapter 19 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 190r–191r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2SA_019_page_001.jpg, 2SA_019_page_002.jpg, 2SA_019_page_003.jpg

---

**19:1** And-it-was-told to-Yo'av, "Behold, the-king [is]-weeping and-mourning over Avshalom."

**19:2** And-became the-victory [ha-teshu'ah] on-that day into-mourning for-all the-people, for the-people heard on-that day, saying, "The-king is-grieved over his-son."

**19:3** And-the-people stole-away [vayyitgannev] on-that day to-come to-the-city, as steal-away [yitgannev] the-people who-are-ashamed [ha-nikh'lamim] when-they-flee in-the-battle.

**19:4** And-the-king covered his-face, and-cried the-king [with] a-great voice, "My-son Avshalom! Avshalom, my-son, my-son!"

**19:5** And-came Yo'av to the-king [to]-the-house and-said, "You-have-put-to-shame [hovashta] this-day [the]-faces of-all your-servants who-saved your-life [nephesh] this-day, and-[the]-life [nephesh] of-your-sons and-your-daughters, and-[the]-life [nephesh] of-your-wives and-[the]-life [nephesh] of-your-concubines,

**19:6** to-love those-who-hate-you and-to-hate those-who-love-you. For you-have-declared this-day that nothing [are]-to-you commanders and-servants. For I-know this-day that if Avshalom [were]-alive and-all-of-us this-day [were]-dead, then right [would it be] in-your-eyes.

**19:7** And-now arise, go-out and-speak upon-[the]-heart of-your-servants. For by-YHWH I-swear, that if-not you [are]-going-out, not a-man will-lodge with-you tonight. And-this [will be]-worse for-you than-all the-evil that has-come upon-you from-your-youth until now."

**19:8** And-arose the-king and-sat in-the-gate. And-to-all the-people they-told, saying, "Behold, the-king [is]-sitting in-the-gate." And-came all the-people before the-king. And-Yisra'el had-fled, each-man to-his-tent [le-ohalav].

**19:9** And-was all the-people contending [nidon] in-all [the]-tribes of-Yisra'el, saying, "The-king delivered-us from-[the]-palm of-our-enemies, and-he saved-us from-[the]-palm of-[the]-Pelishtim, and-now he-has-fled from-the-land from-before Avshalom.

**19:10** And-Avshalom, whom we-anointed over-us, has-died in-the-battle. And-now, why [are]-you silent to-bring-back the-king?"

**19:11** And-the-king David sent to Tsadoq and-to Evyatar the-priests, saying, "Speak to [the]-elders of-Yehudah, saying, 'Why will-you-be [the]-last to-bring-back the-king to his-house?' — And-[the]-word of-all Yisra'el had-come to the-king, to his-house. —

**19:12** 'My-brothers [are]-you, my-bone and-my-flesh [are]-you. And-why will-you-be [the]-last to-bring-back the-king?'

**19:13** And-to-Amasa you-shall-say, 'Are-you-not my-bone and-my-flesh? Thus may-God do to-me and-thus may-he-add, if not commander of-[the]-army you-will-be before-me all the-days, in-place-of Yo'av.'"

**19:14** And-he-turned [vayyat] [the]-heart of-all [the]-men of-Yehudah as-one man, and-they-sent to the-king, "Return, you and-all your-servants."

**19:15** And-returned the-king and-came unto the-Yarden. And-Yehudah came to-the-Gilgal to-go to-meet the-king, to-bring the-king across the-Yarden.

**19:16** And-hurried Shim'i son of-Gera the-Binyamini who [was] from-Bachurim, and-went-down with [the]-men of-Yehudah to-meet the-king David.

**19:17** And-a-thousand men [were]-with-him from-Binyamin. And-Tsiva, servant of-[the]-house of-Sha'ul, and-fifteen his-sons and-twenty his-servants with-him, and-they-rushed [vetsalchu] to-the-Yarden before the-king.

**19:18** And-crossed the-ford [ha-avarah] to-bring-across [the]-house of-the-king and-to-do the-good in-his-eyes. And-Shim'i son of-Gera fell before the-king when-he-was-crossing the-Yarden.

**19:19** And-he-said to the-king, "Let-not my-lord reckon [yachshov] to-me iniquity [avon], and-do-not remember that-which your-servant did-perversely [he'evah] on-the-day that my-lord the-king went-out from-Yerushalayim, for-the-king to-set [it] upon his-heart.

**19:20** For your-servant knows that I sinned. And-behold, I-have-come this-day, first of-all [the]-house of-Yosef, to-go-down to-meet my-lord the-king."

**19:21** And-answered Avishai son of-Tseruyah and-said, "Shall-not for-this Shim'i be-put-to-death, because he-cursed [the]-anointed of-YHWH?"

**19:22** And-said David, "What [is it]-to-me and-to-you, sons of-Tseruyah, that you-should-be to-me this-day as-an-adversary [le-satan]? Shall any-man be-put-to-death this-day in-Yisra'el? For do-I-not know that this-day I [am] king over Yisra'el?"

**19:23** And-said the-king to Shim'i, "You-shall-not die." And-swore to-him the-king.

**19:24** And-Mephiboshet son of-Sha'ul went-down to-meet the-king. And-he-had-not done his-feet [lo-asah raglav] and-had-not done his-mustache [lo-asah sephamo] and-his-garments he-had-not washed, from the-day the-king went until the-day he-came in-peace [be-shalom].

**19:25** And-it-was when-he-came [to]-Yerushalayim to-meet the-king, and-said to-him the-king, "Why did-you-not go with-me, Mephiboshet?"

**19:26** And-he-said, "My-lord the-king, my-servant deceived-me [rimmani]. For your-servant said, 'I-will-saddle for-me the-donkey and-ride upon-it and-go with the-king,' for your-servant [is]-lame [pisseach].

**19:27** And-he-slandered [vayyeraggel] your-servant to my-lord the-king. But-my-lord the-king [is] as-an-angel [mal'akh] of-God; do what [is]-good in-your-eyes.

**19:28** For all [the]-house of-my-father were nothing but men of-death [anshey mavet] before my-lord the-king, and-you-set your-servant among-those-who-eat [at]-your-table. And-what is-there to-me still [a]-right [tsedaqah] even to-cry-out still to the-king?"

**19:29** And-said to-him the-king, "Why do-you-speak still your-words? I-have-said, you and-Tsiva shall-divide the-field."

**19:30** And-said Mephiboshet to the-king, "Even the-whole let-him-take, after that my-lord the-king has-come in-peace [be-shalom] to his-house."

**19:31** And-Barzillai the-Gil'adi went-down from-Roglim and-crossed with the-king [over]-the-Yarden, to-send-him-off [leshalleho] at-the-Yarden.

**19:32** And-Barzillai [was]-very old, a-son of-eighty years. And-he had-provided-for [kilkel] the-king during-his-staying in-Machanayim, for a-man very great [was]-he.

**19:33** And-said the-king to Barzillai, "You cross-over with-me, and-I-will-provide-for-you [vekhilkalti] with-me in-Yerushalayim."

**19:34** And-said Barzillai to the-king, "How-many [are the]-days of-[the]-years of-my-life, that I-should-go-up with the-king to-Yerushalayim?

**19:35** A-son of-eighty years [am]-I this-day. Can-I-discern [ha-eda'] between good and-evil [ben tov le-ra']? Can your-servant taste what I-eat and-what I-drink? Can-I-hear still the-voice of-singing-men [sharim] and-singing-women [sharot]? And-why should-your-servant be still a-burden [le-massa'] upon my-lord the-king?

**19:36** As-a-little [kim'at] your-servant will-cross with the-king [over]-the-Yarden. And-why should-the-king repay-me this recompense [ha-gemulah]?

**19:37** Let-return, please, your-servant, and-let-me-die in-my-city, near [the]-tomb of-my-father and-my-mother. And-behold, your-servant Kimham — let-him cross with my-lord the-king, and-do for-him what [is]-good in-your-eyes."

**19:38** And-said the-king, "With-me will-cross Kimham, and-I will-do for-him the-good in-your-eyes, and-all that you-choose upon-me I-will-do for-you."

**19:39** And-crossed all the-people [over]-the-Yarden, and-the-king crossed. And-kissed the-king Barzillai and-blessed-him, and-he-returned to his-place.

**19:40** And-crossed the-king to-the-Gilgal, and-Kimham crossed with-him. And-all [the]-people of-Yehudah brought the-king across, and-also half [the]-people of-Yisra'el.

**19:41** And-behold, all [the]-men of-Yisra'el [were]-coming to the-king, and-they-said to the-king, "Why have-stolen-you-away [genavukha] our-brothers, [the]-men of-Yehudah, and-brought the-king and-his-household across the-Yarden, and-all [the]-men of-David with-him?"

**19:42** And-answered all [the]-men of-Yehudah upon [the]-men of-Yisra'el, "For near [qarov] [is] the-king to-us. And-why [does]-this anger-you [tichreh]? Eating have-we-eaten [ha-akhol akhalnu] from the-king? Or carrying has-[something]-been-carried [ha-nisse' nissa] to-us?"

**19:43** And-answered [the]-men of-Yisra'el [the]-men of-Yehudah and-said, "Ten portions [yadot] [are]-to-us in-the-king, and-also in-David more-than-you. And-why did-you-treat-us-lightly [heqillotanu]? And-was-not our-word first to-bring-back our-king?" And-harder [was the]-word of-[the]-men of-Yehudah than-[the]-word of-[the]-men of-Yisra'el.

**19:44** [Note: In the Hebrew text (MT), the verse numbering of chapter 19 differs from English versions. The Hebrew 19:1 = English 18:33; the Hebrew 19:44 corresponds to the content that in some English traditions begins chapter 20.]

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.3 — vayyitgannev:** The hitpael of *ganav* (to steal) means "to steal oneself away" — a vivid image of soldiers slinking home like thieves rather than marching triumphantly. The simile likens them to troops ashamed of fleeing, though they have won.

**v.6 — "to love those who hate you":** Joab's rebuke is one of the harshest speeches in the Hebrew Bible. The chiastic structure (*love-hate / hate-love*) makes it rhetorically devastating.

**v.13 — "Are you not my bone and my flesh?":** David uses kinship language (*atsmi u-vesari*) to woo Amasa, Absalom's general, replacing Joab. This is politically astute but will prove fatal for Amasa in chapter 20.

**v.22 — le-satan:** David calls the sons of Zeruiah an "adversary" (*satan*). The word here is a common noun meaning "opponent/accuser," not yet the proper name of a cosmic figure. David refuses to let the day of restoration become a day of execution.

**v.24 — "had not done his feet... had not done his mustache":** Euphemistic expressions for grooming neglect. *Lo-asah raglav* may refer to trimming toenails or washing feet; *lo-asah sephamo* means he had not trimmed his mustache. These are signs of genuine mourning for David's absence.

**v.35 — "Can I discern between good and evil?":** Barzillai's speech is a poignant meditation on aging — the loss of taste, hearing, and discernment. The phrase *ben tov le-ra'* echoes the garden narrative (Gen 2–3), where knowledge of good and evil was the prize; now in old age, that very discernment fades.

**v.43 — "ten portions":** The Hebrew *eser yadot* literally means "ten hands" (i.e., shares). The ten northern tribes claim a larger stake in the king than Judah's two. This dispute is the seed from which Sheba's revolt (ch. 20) and the permanent division of the kingdom (1 Kgs 12) will grow.

*— EMET*
